value: Cardiovascular Thrombotic Events: NSAIDs cause an increased risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic events, including myocardial infarction and stroke, which can be fatal; contraindicated in the setting of CABG surgery.

Gastrointestinal Bleeding, Ulceration, and Perforation: NSAIDs cause an increased risk of serious GI adverse events including bleeding, ulceration, and perforation of the stomach or intestines, which can be fatal.

refs.quote: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) cause an increased risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic events, including myocardial infarction, and stroke, which can be fatal. This risk may occur early in the treatment and may increase with duration of use [see Warnings and Precautions (5.1) ] .
NSAIDs cause an increased risk of serious gastrointestinal (GI) adverse events including bleeding, ulceration, and perforation of the stomach or intestines, which can be fatal.
The mechanism of action of CELEBREX is believed to be due to inhibition of prostaglandin synthesis, primarily via inhibition of COX-2.

mg_safety.note: Selective COX-2 inhibitor NSAID; no neuromuscular junction blocking warnings.

value.instructions: For patients who have difficulty swallowing capsules, the entire capsule contents can be carefully emptied onto a level teaspoon of cool or room temperature applesauce and ingested immediately with water (stable up to 6 hours refrigerated at 2°C to 8°C).

refs.quote: For patients who have difficulty swallowing capsules, the contents of a CELEBREX capsule can be added to applesauce. The entire capsule contents are carefully emptied onto a level teaspoon of cool or room temperature applesauce and ingested immediately with water.

pgx.value: In adult patients known or suspected to be CYP2C9 poor metabolizers (e.g., CYP2C9*3/*3, which have 3- to 7-fold higher systemic levels), initiate treatment with half of the lowest recommended dose. In JRA patients who are CYP2C9 poor metabolizers, consider alternative treatments.

refs.quote: In patients who are known or suspected to be poor CYP2C9 metabolizers (i.e., CYP2C9*3/*3), based on genotype or previous history/experience with other CYP2C9 substrates (such as warfarin, phenytoin) administer CELEBREX starting with half the lowest recommended dose. Alternative management should be considered in JRA patients identified to be CYP2C9 poor metabolizers

mechanism_of_action.value: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug with analgesic, anti-inflammatory, and antipyretic properties; inhibits prostaglandin synthesis primarily via selective inhibition of COX-2.

refs.quote: Celecoxib has analgesic, anti-inflammatory, and antipyretic properties. The mechanism of action of CELEBREX is believed to be due to inhibition of prostaglandin synthesis, primarily via inhibition of COX-2.
Celecoxib metabolism is primarily mediated via CYP2C9.

In vitro studies indicate that celecoxib, although not a substrate, is an inhibitor of CYP2D6. Therefore, there is a potential for an in vivo drug interaction with drugs that are metabolized by CYP2D6 (e.g., atomoxetine), and celecoxib may enhance the exposure and toxicity of these drugs.

value.drug_or_class: Drugs that Interfere with Hemostasis (Anticoagulants, Antiplatelets, SSRIs, SNRIs)
value.effect: Synergistic effect on bleeding with warfarin/anticoagulants; SSRIs/SNRIs may potentiate NSAID bleeding risk.
value.management: Monitor patients with concomitant use of CELEBREX with anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), antiplatelet drugs (e.g., aspirin), SSRIs, and SNRIs for signs of bleeding.

refs.quote: Monitor patients with concomitant use of CELEBREX with anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), antiplatelet drugs (e.g., aspirin), SSRIs, and SNRIs for signs of bleeding [see Warnings and Precautions (5.12) ] .

value.effect: Significantly increases GI adverse reactions and bleeding risk without greater therapeutic effect (celecoxib 200-400 mg/day did not interfere with cardioprotective antiplatelet effect of aspirin 100-325 mg).
value.management: Concomitant use of CELEBREX and analgesic doses of aspirin is not generally recommended.

refs.quote: Concomitant use of CELEBREX and analgesic doses of aspirin is not generally recommended because of the increased risk of bleeding [see Warnings and Precautions (5.12) ] .

value.effect: May diminish antihypertensive effect; co-administration with ACE inhibitors or ARBs in elderly, volume-depleted, or renally impaired patients may cause deterioration of renal function including acute renal failure.
value.management: Monitor blood pressure; in elderly, volume-depleted, or renally impaired patients, ensure adequate hydration and monitor renal function at baseline and periodically.

refs.quote: During concomitant use of CELEBREX and ACE inhibitors or ARBs in patients who are elderly, volume-depleted, or have impaired renal function, monitor for signs of worsening renal function [see Warnings and Precautions (5.6) ] .

value.effect: Reduces natriuretic effect of loop (e.g., furosemide) and thiazide diuretics.
value.management: Observe patients for signs of worsening renal function and assure diuretic efficacy including antihypertensive effects.

refs.quote: During concomitant use of CELEBREX with diuretics, observe patients for signs of worsening renal function, in addition to assuring diuretic efficacy including antihypertensive effects [see Warnings and Precautions (5.6) ] .

value.effect: Increases serum concentration and prolongs half-life of digoxin.
value.management: Monitor serum digoxin levels during concomitant use.

refs.quote: During concomitant use of CELEBREX and digoxin, monitor serum digoxin levels.

value.effect: Elevates plasma lithium levels (+17% in celecoxib study) and reduces renal lithium clearance (~20%).
value.management: Monitor patients for signs of lithium toxicity during concomitant use.

refs.quote: During concomitant use of CELEBREX and lithium, monitor patients for signs of lithium toxicity.

value.effect: May increase risk for methotrexate toxicity (neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, renal dysfunction).
value.management: Monitor patients for methotrexate toxicity during concomitant use.

refs.quote: During concomitant use of CELEBREX and methotrexate, monitor patients for methotrexate toxicity.

value.management: Monitor patients for signs of worsening renal function.

refs.quote: During concomitant use of CELEBREX and cyclosporine, monitor patients for signs of worsening renal function.

value.effect: Increases risk of GI toxicity with little or no increase in efficacy.
value.management: Concomitant use of Celecoxib with other NSAIDs or salicylates is not recommended.

refs.quote: The concomitant use of Celecoxib with other NSAIDs or salicylates is not recommended.

value.effect: May increase risk of pemetrexed-associated myelosuppression, renal, and GI toxicity.
value.management: In patients with CrCl 45 to 79 mL/min, monitor for myelosuppression, renal, and GI toxicity.

refs.quote: During concomitant use of CELEBREX and pemetrexed, in patients with renal impairment whose creatinine clearance ranges from 45 to 79 mL/min, monitor for myelosuppression, renal and GI toxicity.

value.drug_or_class: CYP2C9 Inhibitors or Inducers (e.g., fluconazole, rifampin)
value.effect: CYP2C9 inhibitors (e.g., fluconazole, 2-fold increase) enhance exposure and toxicity of celecoxib; CYP2C9 inducers (e.g., rifampin) may compromise efficacy.
value.management: Evaluate patient medical history; a dosage adjustment may be warranted when administered with CYP2C9 inhibitors or inducers.

refs.quote: A dosage adjustment may be warranted when celecoxib is administered with CYP2C9 inhibitors or inducers [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.3) ] .

value.effect: Celecoxib inhibits CYP2D6 and may enhance exposure and toxicity of CYP2D6 substrates.
value.management: Evaluate patient medical history; a dosage adjustment may be warranted when administered with CYP2D6 substrates.

refs.quote: A dosage adjustment may be warranted when celecoxib is administered with CYP2D6 substrates [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.3) ] .

value.effect: Concomitant use may increase risk of GI ulceration or bleeding.
value.management: Monitor patients with concomitant use of CELEBREX with corticosteroids for signs of bleeding.

refs.quote: Monitor patients with concomitant use of CELEBREX with corticosteroids for signs of bleeding [see Warnings and Precautions (5.2) ] .

tier.note: Avoid use at about 30 weeks gestation and later due to premature closure of fetal ductus arteriosus; limit dose/duration at >=20 weeks due to oligohydramnios/neonatal renal impairment (monitor with ultrasound if >48 hours). Animal studies showed ventricular septal defects (2x MRHD), diaphragmatic hernias (6x MRHD), and pre/post-implantation losses; associated with reversible female infertility.

refs.quote: Because of these risks, limit dose and duration of CELEBREX use between about 20 and 30 weeks of gestation and avoid CELEBREX use at about 30 weeks of gestation and later in pregnancy (see Clinical Considerations , Data ) .

contraception.value: Does not alter hormonal contraceptive efficacy, though chronic periconceptional COX-2 inhibition may reversibly delay ovulation; discontinue if difficulty conceiving.

refs.quote: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs do not interact with hormonal contraceptives, though chronic periconceptional COX inhibition can reversibly delay ovulation and impair implantation; discontinue in patients experiencing difficulty conceiving.
